item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
655
ABPZ20 KNHC 040516
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sat Oct 3 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Nolo, located well to the west-northwest of the main Hawaiian
Islands, and on Hurricane Rachel, located a few hundred miles
southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
A broad area of low pressure is forecast to develop over the next
day or so just to the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is expected to form during the middle to
latter portion of the week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward, just offshore of the southern
to southwestern coast of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM MST Sun Oct 04 2026
 
...RACHEL STRENGTHENS A LITTLE MORE WHILE IT MOVES 
WEST-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.2N 113.2W
ABOUT 280 MI...455 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...968 MB...28.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 20.2 North, longitude 113.2 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west-northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h).  A turn toward the
west is expected later today, and a westward motion with some
increase in forward speed is expected through Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are now near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Fluctuations in strength are possible through tonight. 
Rachel is expected to slowly weaken starting on Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 968 mb (28.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast
of west-central Mexico through the weekend and the Baja California
Peninsula through Monday. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Sun Oct 04 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 040834
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM MST Sun Oct 04 2026

Satellite imagery shows that Rachel has continued to get better 
organized since the last advisory. While the eye is not very clear 
at this time, the eyewall cloud tops have become more symmetric with 
some cloud top temperatures colder than -80C. The various satellite 
intensity estimates are in the 76-104 kt range, and they have all 
trended upward over the past six hours. Based on this, the initial 
intensity is increased to 85 kt.

The initial motion is now 295/4 kt. A turn toward the west with 
some increase in forward speed is expected during the next 72 h as 
a mid-level ridge to the north of the hurricane strengthens a bit. 
After 72 h, a mid-latitude trough approaching from the west will 
create a break in the ridge near 130-135W, and Rachel is expected 
to turn west-northwestward again as it approaches the break. The 
new forecast track has only minor adjustments from the previous 
track, and it lies close to the center of the fairly well clustered 
track guidance.

Sea surface temperature analyses indicate that Rachel should be 
crossing Polo's cold wake right now. The current development trend 
is not consistent with this, though. During the next 24 h, the 
hurricane should move over slightly warmer water that in theory 
should allow some strengthening. However, none of the intensity 
guidance shows any additional strengthening during this time. Given 
these mixed signals, the new intensity forecast will show a steady 
intensity for 12 h, followed by a gradual weakening based on the 
intensity guidance trends. Rachel should encounter a drier air 
mass and reach water temperatures of 25-26C starting in about 72 h, 
but during this time the forecast wind shear becomes quite light. 
This may allow the cyclone to develop annular characteristics, 
which would at least slow any weakening. Overall, the intensity 
forecast is near the upper edge of the guidance.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
